properties.description:
The second check `req:design-dependencies-declared` names and only half-delivered. A dependency declaration that names another reflow2 design may also name that design's COMMITTED EXPORT; reflow2 records the export's content hash when the declaration is made, and later reads report whether the upstream has moved since.

SERVED AS `upstream_status`, and carried on `loop_status` as `upstream_moved` — the same shape `record_moved` already has, and for the same reason: that is the orientation call the session-start hook points sessions at. Deliberately NOT folded into `sync_status`, which answers the other direction (has MY record moved) and would blur two different questions into one list.

📌 THE NEAR-MATCH OFFERED WAS `chg:a-declared-dependency-can-be-watched-without-being-imported`, which is the EVENT of building this on 2026-08-26. This is the standing CAPABILITY.

⭐ WHY IT IS NOT THE EXISTING MECHANISM. `provenance::last_synced` already answers "has that file moved", but the only two paths that write into it are `export_graph` and `import_graph` — and importing a design into a store that already holds one KEEPS THE HOST'S NAME and upserts the incoming nodes into it. So watching a child by importing it ABSORBS the child, which is exactly what the hub case says a hub must not do. This watches without taking.

⭐ THE CHILD LIST IS THE COMMITTED MANIFEST, not a per-machine config. `reflow2.toml` already names each dependency's design by `graph_id`, version-pinned and reviewable in a diff, and it inherits the direction the dependency edge carries.

🛑 IT MUST NOT SILENCE ITSELF. The baseline is taken at DECLARATION time and a read never touches it — a check that refreshed what it compares against would report `moved` once and then be permanently quiet. Re-declaring is the acknowledgement (`dec:ask-not-repair`).

WHAT IT REPORTS, and absence is reported rather than assumed: `moved`, `unchanged`, `never_seen` (a path is declared and nobody has looked yet), `missing`, `unreadable`, `graph_id_mismatch` (the export at that path belongs to a different design than the one declared), `not_watched` (a dependency names another design but gives nothing to watch) and `not_observed` (the bounded pass did not open it). Only `moved`, `missing`, `unreadable` and `graph_id_mismatch` reach `loop_status`'s `next` list.

⚠️ THE PLACEMENT IS THE DESIGN. `reflow2-core` does no file I/O, so the core holds the declarations and the COMPARISON and the caller supplies what it found on disk — the same split `reconcile_dependencies` and `reconcile_artifacts` already make. The reading lives at the MCP layer in `upstream.rs`, beside `sync_debt`, for the reason that module already states. It does not NAVIGATE: every path read is one this design pointed at itself, in its own committed manifest.

⚠️ CHEAP WHEN UNUSED. `loop_status` gates on the manifest, so a design declaring no upstream export — every design until somebody deliberately points at one, this one included — pays a single node scan and reads no files. The pass is bounded at 16 exports and NAMES what it skipped.

⚠️ WHAT IT DOES NOT DELIVER. A declaration says I DEPEND ON that; a hub says I AM ANSWERABLE FOR that. Where a hub merely owns a child, saying so as a dependency would be modelling fiction. Cross-design realization and verification roll-up are untouched, and so is decisions-inherit-downward.

═══ 2026-09-27 — WATCHED AT THE SERVER THAT HOLDS IT (req:a-design-watches-another-design-at-the-server-that-holds-it) ═══
A declaration may now name `design_address` instead of an export path: the server holding the design (flo2's https://api.flo2.io/g/<id>/mcp, an organisation's reflow2, or a local one). Under the design-and-export rules an export is a copy nothing tracks, so the address is where the design is watched.
- THE READ: the MCP handshake, then `export_graph` with no path, then the COMPUTED content hash (upstream::fingerprint). This is the same fingerprint a file watch takes, so a baseline means the same thing either way. The key is the one `reflow2-mcp setup` stored for that server's origin, and nothing else.
- WHERE IT RUNS: at declaration (the baseline, taken before the write lock) and in `upstream_status`. `loop_status` never goes over the network: an address watch there is `not_observed` and names `upstream_status` as where it is read.
- NEW STATES: `unreachable` (no answer, a server error, a timeout) and `refused` (401/403/404, a tool refusal, a key refused over plain http). Both are actionable and neither ever reads as `unchanged`. The report's note stops saying "none moved" when any target could not be read.
- HOSTED SERVERS DO NOT REACH OUT: a `--registry-root` server (ReflowService::without_reaching_out) records an address watch and reports it `refused`, so a caller cannot make a server holding other people's designs contact a host of the caller's choosing.
- ONE PLACE: a declaration naming both `design_address` and `design_export` is refused, in the core and in the tool before any network call.
- ALSO FIXED: all three watch readers now require an IDENTIFIED design (fact:the-upstream-watch-read-any-json-object-as-a-design-2026-09-27).
- COST, stated: every read transfers the whole design. A cheap fingerprint read on the server would replace it; flo2's gateway would then need to offer that tool.
properties.name: A design says when the design it depends on has moved, without importing it
